back2basics.text: A Strategic Partnership is a formal agreement between countries to cooperate closely on multiple fronts such as defence, trade, technology, and culture. It involves high-level political dialogue, institutional cooperation, and shared goals to enhance mutual interests and regional stability. Such partnerships often include joint action plans with timelines and specific sectors for collaboration.

back2basics.text: Monetary policy uses instruments like Treasury Bills and Variable Rate Repo auctions to regulate liquidity and control interest rates. back2basics.text: An election petition is a legal challenge to the validity of an election result. Under Indian law, such petitions must be filed within a strict time frame, typically 45 days from the date of election, to ensure timely resolution and finality. This limitation period is prescribed by special election laws and overrides general rules on limitation calculation.

2026-10-23-am-441de7d03c.deck: The Madras High Court recently heard arguments on the timeliness of an election petition challenging Udhayanidhi Stalin's 2026 Assembly election victory. This case highlights important legal provisions on election petition filing deadlines and the judiciary's role in electoral dispute resolution.

body.label: 45-day limitation period
body.text: Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 mandates that election petitions must be filed within 45 days from the date of election of the returned candidate.

body.label: No exclusion of first day
body.text: The court held that the principle of excluding the first day for limitation calculation, as per the General Clauses Act, 1897, does not apply to election petitions, making the limitation period start on the election date itself.

body.label: Consequences of delay
body.text: Section 86 of the 1951 Act requires the High Court to dismiss election petitions filed after the limitation period.

back2basics.text: An earthquake is the shaking of the Earth's surface caused by the sudden release of energy in the crust, often along fault lines. Magnitude measures the energy released, while the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the origin. Earthquakes can cause damage to infrastructure and loss of life, especially in mountainous and densely populated areas. Disaster management involves preparedness, response, and recovery to reduce the impact of such natural hazards.

body.label: Campaign objective
body.text: The Khet Bachao Abhiyan is a nationwide public awareness campaign running from 22 October to 30 November 2026 to promote balanced fertiliser use and soil health among farmers.

body.label: Soil health concerns
body.text: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan warned that unbalanced use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides harms soil fertility and human health, making soil barren and bodies prone to diseases.

body.label: Key measures for farmers
body.text: Farmers are encouraged to use Soil Health Cards to apply fertilisers as per need, adopt crop rotation to improve soil nutrients, and start natural farming on at least half an acre using organic inputs like Beejamrit and Ghanjeevamrit.

body.label: Support for rural poor
body.text: The government approved ₹1,343 crore to build 28,422 permanent houses for poor families in Haryana under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin.

body.label: Concept of AgriVoltaics
body.text: AgriVoltaics integrates solar panels above agricultural land, allowing crops to grow beneath while generating electricity, thus using the same land for dual purposes.

body.label: Benefits for small farmers
body.text: The policy focuses on benefiting 85% of small and marginal farmers by designing solar installations that do not disrupt farming and allow crop choice and rotation.

body.label: Economic and environmental impact
body.text: AgriVoltaics can increase crop yields by 10-20%, generate clean energy to meet India's electricity demand by 2050, and create about 3.32 lakh full-time local jobs, especially for rural youth.

body.label: Government initiatives
body.text: The next phase of PM-KUSUM will launch the world's largest AgriVoltaics campaign, with cooperation between Agriculture and New & Renewable Energy Ministries.

sections.heading: What is AgriVoltaics and its significance for farmers?

body.label: State-level policies
body.text: States like Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Bihar are formulating policies and incentives to promote agrivoltaic projects tailored to local agriculture.

body.label: Infrastructure and training
body.text: States are strengthening grid infrastructure, solarising agricultural tubewells, and proposing farmer training through Krishi Vigyan Kendras and agricultural universities.

body.label: Investment and finance
body.text: Discussions at the conference included blended finance mechanisms, risk mitigation, and concessional lending to attract private investment in agrivoltaics.

body.label: Farmer rights and land use
body.text: Policies ensure farmer land ownership protection, require cultivable land to remain productive, and allow farmers to own or lease land while continuing cultivation.

back2basics.concept: Banking Regulation Act and RBI's supervisory role
back2basics.text: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949, empowers the Reserve Bank of India to regulate and supervise banking institutions, including cooperative banks. Sections 35A and 56 allow RBI to issue directions to banks to protect depositors' interests and ensure financial stability. Cooperative banks are financial entities owned and operated by their members, often serving local communities, and require regulatory oversight to maintain sound governance and liquidity.

These actions highlight RBI's role in supervising cooperative banks to protect depositors and maintain financial stability.

body: RBI uses Sections 35A and 56 to issue directions restricting bank operations when financial health is weak.

body.label: Operational restrictions
body.text: From October 21, 2026, the bank cannot grant or renew loans, make investments, incur liabilities, accept fresh deposits, or dispose of assets without RBI's prior written approval.

body.label: Withdrawal limits
body.text: Depositors can withdraw up to ₹5,000 from their accounts, and the bank may set off loans against deposits under specified conditions.

body.label: Essential expenditures allowed
body.text: The bank may pay for essential items such as employee salaries, rent, and electricity bills as per RBI directions.

body.label: Reason for directions
body.text: RBI issued these directions due to the bank's poor liquidity and inadequate efforts to address supervisory concerns, aiming to protect depositors.

body.label: Deposit insurance
body.text: Depositors are entitled to insurance claims up to ₹5,00,000 from the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) after verification.

body.label: License status
body.text: These directions do not mean cancellation of the bank's license; the bank continues operations under restrictions until its financial position improves.

body.label: Biomass utilization
body.text: Compliance with CAQM Direction No. 92 mandates use of paddy straw-based biomass pellets/briquettes in brick kilns and biomass co-firing in thermal power plants.

back2basics.patternId: Digital public infrastructure and AI governance
back2basics.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) involves computer systems performing tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as learning and decision-making. Data centres are facilities that house computer systems and associated components to store and process data. Large data centres support training of complex AI models, while smaller, distributed data centres can perform inference tasks closer to end-users, improving efficiency and reducing resource consumption.

2026-10-23-am-d7afe4bc42.deck: IIT-Madras announced research projects on artificial intelligence including a feasibility study for small, frugal data centres called pico centres. This matters for UPSC aspirants as it highlights India's approach to AI development, resource-efficient technology, and responsible AI governance.

body: IIT-Madras is studying small, energy-efficient data centres called pico centres to support AI inference across sectors.
The Bodhan AI initiative aims to provide personalized AI education to millions of students using frugal AI infrastructure.
CeRAI's efforts in responsible AI governance include creating case studies and evaluation platforms to ensure accountability.
These initiatives demonstrate how frugal engineering can make AI accessible, sustainable, and trustworthy in India.
structure.conclusion: Frugal engineering at IIT-Madras exemplifies a practical approach to AI development and governance aligned with India's needs.
structure.intro: Frugal engineering focuses on developing cost-effective and resource-efficient technologies.

body.label: Frugal AI data centres
body.text: IIT-Madras plans to study the feasibility of small, distributed 'pico centres' that consume less electricity and resources, supporting inference tasks across sectors like agriculture, space, manufacturing, health, and law.

body.label: Bodhan AI initiative
body.text: Bodhan AI, a Centre of Excellence for AI in Education funded by the Union Ministry of Education and incubated at IIT-Madras, is working on frugal AI data centres to provide personalized AI tutors to 25 crore school students in India.

body.label: Responsible AI efforts
body.text: The Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI) at IIT-Madras, in partnership with The Better India, will produce 500 videos showcasing case studies on responsible and effective AI use.

body.label: AI evaluation platform
body.text: IIT-Madras launched a software platform to evaluate AI tools using over 50 metrics and 100 sub-metrics in multiple languages.

body.label: Trusted AI Commons
body.text: Work will begin on a Trusted AI Commons to enhance AI accountability and responsibility.

sections.heading: What AI research projects did IIT-Madras announce?

body.label: Energy efficiency
body.text: Small data centres, developed with frugal engineering, consume less electricity and resources compared to large data centres used for training large language models.

body.label: Distributed model
body.text: A federated and distributed model of pico centres can serve diverse end-user groups effectively across multiple sectors.

body.label: Sectoral applications
body.text: These centres can support inference tasks in agriculture, space, manufacturing, health, law, and education, making AI more accessible and practical.

body.label: Accountability frameworks
body.text: The Trusted AI Commons initiative aims to improve AI accountability and responsibility.

body.label: Evaluation metrics
body.text: The AI evaluation platform assesses tools on extensive metrics to ensure quality and trustworthiness.
